recent_reviews.body: What an absolute joke. Charged me $39 just to have a so called provider “review” my health history. It did not include any medication which was stated on their website ad that the $39 did include my first month. Don’t be fooled by their lies. It’s $149-299 per month for Zepbound plus $139 per month just to have a subscription so you can “message” a provider. It’s cheaper just to bite the bullet and pay cash at your local pharmacy. This is a goat rope joke of a company that is very deceitful with their billing practices. I have reported the $39 dollar charge as fraud on my credit card because that’s exactly what it was. A big fraud!

recent_reviews.title: Buyer Beware
recent_reviews.body: Buyer Beware. Malpractice My experience with Hims Weight Loss has been deeply disappointing and raises serious concerns regarding continuity of care. I enrolled in and paid for a 360-day weight loss program, completed all required intake forms, check-ins, and program requirements, and followed the prescribed treatment plan exactly as directed. The problem began when Hims failed to ship a scheduled medication refill. As my medication supply ran out, I repeatedly contacted support seeking assistance to maintain continuity of treatment. What followed was a revolving door of customer service representatives and physicians. Over multiple interactions, I was required to repeatedly explain my situation to new providers who appeared unfamiliar with the history of my case. Despite numerous messages, no single provider or case manager assumed ownership of the issue. Rather than addressing the immediate problem of maintaining continuity of treatment, discussions shifted toward changing medications, pricing alternatives, and partial refunds. While refunds may address financial concerns, they do not address the interruption of a medical treatment plan already in progress. My concern is not merely customer service. It is continuity of care, care coordination, and accountability. I encourage prospective customers to carefully consider whether a highly distributed telehealth model with multiple rotating providers is consistent with their expectations for ongoing medical management. This review reflects my personal experience and is supported by documented communications with Hims.

recent_reviews.title: Horrible customer service
recent_reviews.body: So unbelievably disappointed with this company and how they handle any problem. I call customer service about an email I received saying my account was cancelled right after they charged me $149.99 for my medication which was never sent. Confused I called and waited an hour on hold. Was greeted by a person who could barely speak English and the communication was totally scripted and useless. When I asked for a supervisor I was placed on hold for another 44 minutes just to be hung up on. So I called back waited another 37 minutes on hold and this time got a little information about a duplicate account that was created and was removed but assured that everything thing was fine and still active. When I explain my frustration with all the waiting and BS with customer service I was considering canceling my account so she cancelled it before I even got through with our conversation. It was the most frustrating and ridiculous process. They would not refund my money for the exam but they refunded me for the meds. I asked for my medical eval and the scrip that I was approved for and they have refused to send anything to me. I paid $39!to get assessed and provided a script for the meds yet they refuse to provide them to me and refuse to refund me for that service. Why should I pay anything if your not giving me what I paid for. This company is trash and once they have a hook in you don’t expect any help resolving any concerns your might have.
